text.p: Following are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Free trade agreement on agricultural products between the Baltic states came into effect on January 1. Latvian food processing companies see that as a prospect of extending their businesses. Laima, one of the biggset confectionery firms in Latvia, expects to increase its exports to Lithuania nine times and sees a 2.5-fold increase of exports to Estonia.

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele called 1997 a watershed year for the Latvian state, a test of its ability to perform, in his New Year's TV-address. 1996 was the first, after the regained independence, when widespread theft was stopped, he noted. "We will not have another Lata International, Banka Baltija, another G-24 credit," he said, referring to the most notorious shady transactions in recent years.
- Electric energy tariffs are likely to be increased by seven to eight percent on average as of March 1.

- The Diena is the most subscribed of Latvian dailies with 33,957 subscribers, an increase of 4000. It is followed by the Neatkariga Rita Avize (12,876) and the Rigas Balss (10,563). Among weeklies the Lauku Avize continues with its unrivaled lead in yers with 105,551 subsribers.

- Opinion poll by Prognoze ranks Prime Minister Andris Shkele as the most popular politician, followed by President Guntis Ulmanis. The passing of balanced 1997 budget by parliament is viewed as the most important event of 1996, the poll shows.
